newsitem.title: USA: Folgers to raise coffee prices more and sooner.
newsitem.headline: Folgers to raise coffee prices more and sooner.

text.p: Coffee drinkers should get ready for a bigger jolt -- at the checkout counter.

Folgers Coffee Co. said Thursday it will raise its retail coffee prices by up to 45 cents a can as of March 3 -- a bigger hike and sooner than announced previously -- as green coffee prices have risen further.
The Procter & Gamble unit said the list price on its standard 13-ounce can of coffee will rise by 45 cents, triple the 15-cent increase announced Feb. 10, bringing the price tag to $2.71.
The increase will take effect on March 3, two weeks earlier than previously announced.
"The market increase has accelerated in recent days, triggering our most recent revision," Folgers said in a statement.

Green coffee prices have risen since January due to limited supplies of Central American coffees, a drop in size estimates for the next Brazil coffee crop, dock strikes and threatened growers' strikes in Colombia, Folgers said. The Association of Coffee Producing Countries also said they plan to limit exports, it added.
Folgers quadrupled its increase on the list price of its 13-ounce can of decaffeinated coffee to 40 cents from the 10 cents announced Feb. 10, to $3.41.
Instant coffee will go up 2.50 cents an ounce rather than the 1.25 cents previously announced to $3.76 per eight-ounce can.
Folgers "Singles" packet coffee will cost the same for the time being as this line has a different blend and processing method than ground Folgers coffee, the company said.
Procter & Gamble's stock fell $2 to $125.125 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon.
